machine: Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (40 CUs, RDNA3.5) / XDNA2, 128 GB, CachyOS, Linux 7.3.4
gpu_driver: Mesa 26.2.6 RADV (KHR_coopmat, wave64); power profile balanced; GPU held about 2.8 GHz at about 128 W during prefill
model: Qwen3.8-27B UD-IQ3_S (qwen35: 48 Gated DeltaNet + 16 attention layers)
prompt: docs/results/headline-models-2026-10-21/qwen38-27b.json request: 2,769 tokens, cache_prompt false, 16 reply tokens

backends.release: llama.cpp b10944 Linux Vulkan release, libggml-vulkan.so sha256 c25c5ac2bed23bc11351b51f2303084be82c9d1419061c9fae1bfd938b869e06
backends.patched: same release with libggml-vulkan.so from tools/build-vulkan.sh (patches/llama.cpp-b10944/vulkan-rdna3-prefill.patch); final build sha256 07f0a3319573a2b24aabfc01b0fb470f7c6c9d091ac6661bfe48db7571aece51. Earlier tables used builds from earlier steps of the same patch

changes: RDNA3 coopmat matmul on GPUs with 32 or more compute units: shared-memory row pad 2 instead of 4 (8-byte aligned rows, more workgroups per WGP)

RDNA3 coopmat quant matmul on GPUs with 32 or more compute units: extra 128x256 tile where 512 threads multiply and 256 producer threads load and dequantize the next tile into a second buffer; chosen unless padding N to 256 costs more than 15% beyond padding it to 128
The 128x128 coopmat quant tile also gets 256 producer threads on those GPUs: IQ2_S +20-22% (22-24 to 27-28 TFLOPS), shapes that pick it (128 or 384 tokens) +4% to +40%, others unchanged

Wider weight loaders for every GPU: IQ3_S, IQ3_XXS and IQ4_XS unpack 8 values per call instead of 4, Q4_K and Q5_K 8 instead of 4, Q3_K and Q6_K 4 instead of 2, sharing the scale, sign and index work. Same arithmetic, so results are identical (perplexity 1.8734 before and after). Kernel gains on the 8060S: IQ3_S +3-8%, IQ3_XXS +1-4%, IQ4_XS about 0, Q3_K +13%, Q4_K +8-14%, Q5_K +3%, Q6_K +9%
Shared-memory check counts the coopmat stage per consumer subgroup, so tiles that do not fit (IQ2_S, IQ1 lookup tables) fall back
CONCAT on dim 0 with a transposed second input (Gated DeltaNet conv state + activations) runs as two copies, the second through the tiled transpose copy
On UMA, tensor reads take the CPU memcpy shortcut only from host-cached memory; uncached device memory is copied by the GPU into cached staging first (llama.cpp master has the same fix for AMD)
zest launcher: on a Radeon 8060S or 8050S it adds -dev Vulkan0 and, for chat programs, -ub 256 -b 2048

server.method: llama-server with Lemonade's command line (--ctx-size 8192 --device Vulkan0 --jinja --metrics -ts 1 -b 2048 --flash-attn on --parallel 1, -ub as listed), one warm-up then 3 requests per start, two alternating rounds inside dibs run --measure (CLEAN before and after). lemond itself was not run: its libwebsockets dependency is missing on this install
server.reply: identical text in every run: "A harbor town's decline from a bustling trade hub to a quiet fishing spot was"
server.earlier_unquiet_sitting: release ub 2048 281.6; patched ub 2048 421.3; patched ub 256 464.2 (not CLEAN-checked; the release's figure moves most between sittings)

release_ubatch_sitting.method: second dibs run --measure sitting (CLEAN before and after), release backend only, alternating ubatch
release_ubatch_sitting.note: what the launcher's -ub 256 gives without the patched Vulkan backend

installed_final_build.method: third_party/llama-b10944 with the final libggml-vulkan.so (the folder Lemonade's config runs), dibs run --measure, CLEAN
installed_final_build.reply: same text as every other run

final_build.method: third_party/llama-b10944 with the final SDK-built libggml-vulkan.so, -ub 256, dibs run --measure CLEAN
final_build.correctness: test-backend-ops with this exact library: full suite 19943/19943 (MUL_MAT 2184, MUL_MAT_ID 921, CONCAT 320 among them)

wider_loaders.method: third_party/llama-b10944 with the patched library, -ub 256 unless noted, dibs run --measure CLEAN
wider_loaders.note: separate sittings; the second adds only K-quant loader changes, so the difference is sitting-to-sitting variation

context_checkpoints.what: llama-server saves the recurrent state (149.6 MiB) twice near the end of each prompt so later turns can resume
context_checkpoints.release_cause: CPU memcpy from uncached (write-combined) device-local memory, about 125 MB/s

llama_bench.method: llama-bench -dev Vulkan0 -fa on -b 2048, same sitting per table

matmul_tflops.method: test-backend-ops perf, MUL_MAT f32 activations, n = 2048 tokens unless stated
matmul_tflops.ceiling_probe: with global loads removed the coopmat loop reached 33-35 TFLOPS (f16 accumulate) and 34-39 (f32); peak WMMA at 2.8 GHz is about 57

profile_patched_ub256: GPU time: matmul 86.6%, GLU 3.2%, flash attention 2.4%, RMS norm 2.0%, Gated DeltaNet 1.7%, everything else under 1.1% each

correctness.mul_mat: 2184/2184 passed, including local cases that pick the new tile for every quant type, with ragged edges

npu: Not used on Strix Halo: NPU-assisted prefill measured 221-255 tokens/s against 258-300 for the release GPU alone (halo-zest-qwen38-27b-2026-11-13.json), and the patched GPU is faster still. hipfire independently found no net gain from GPU+NPU co-op prefill on this chip.
explored_without_gain: f32 instead of f16 accumulation: removes 128 half-register copies per 32 matrix ops but measured a tie at -ub 256 (464 vs 465) and +1.6% at 2048
other tile shapes for the producer kernel (256 consumers of 128x64, 64x128 per warp, 128 producers, 64x256 tiles): all within about 1% or slower

two-tile register prefetch of IQ3_S raw blocks in the producers: the 768-thread workgroup caps waves at 120 VGPRs and the 128x256 shaders already need 118, so the prefetch spilled and ran at 6-19 TFLOPS
wave32 compute (RDNA3 default subgroup size 32): no change

producers and consumers in separate loops (warp specialization) with two-tile prefetch: no spills (112 VGPRs) but IQ3_S 6% slower; unpacking costs vector-unit and shared-memory throughput, not latency
ROCm/HIP backend (see rocm_comparison): 385 tok/s through the server against 454-473 for the patched Vulkan backend
headroom: With producers idle after the first tile the consumers reach 33-36 TFLOPS against 28-30 in full: unpacking the weights is the limit, and the register file blocks deeper prefetch in this kernel design

rocm_comparison.backend: lemonade-sdk/llamacpp-rocm b1376 (llama.cpp 4f2187e, ROCm 10.3.0a20261113, gfx1151 only), the build Lemonade's llamacpp_backend rocm uses; llama.cpp's own b10944 ROCm 10.0 release needs a system ROCm, which this machine lacks

server.method: llama-server with Lemonade's arguments (--device ROCm0 for ROCm), dibs run --measure, CLEAN, two alternating rounds

rocm_comparison.conclusion: ROCm needs no patch and beats the release Vulkan backend (385 against about 322 through the server), but the patched Vulkan backend is about 18% faster still

llama_cpp_master_comparison.conclusion: master's gains over b10944 are a ~5% faster matmul (its new int8 coopmat path and other changes) and under 1% from fused norms; the patched b10944 matmul is well ahead, so porting the patch to master would add about 1% here. The patch does not apply to master as is (all four files changed)
